workarounds.symptom: Setting a logpoint right after a navigation can fail with "No parsed script" (flaky LogpointManager tests)
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix: wait for parsed scripts before reporting an unknown logpoint URL. Target files: src/LogpointManager.ts. Setting a logpoint right after a navigation can fail with `No parsed script or original source file matches "…"`. This is what makes the `LogpointManager` tests flaky (see the runs listed in #3460). (Ref: https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp/pull/3461)

workarounds.symptom: Query_heapsnapshot_objects fails with an internal TypeError when className is not a valid regular expression
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix: validate heap snapshot className regex. Target files: src/config/cli-options.ts, src/processors/HeapSnapshotManager.ts, src/tools/memory.ts. Invalid `className` or `propertyName` regular expressions can produce an internal `serializeItemsRange` TypeError. Validate both patterns before loading the heap snapshot and report an error identifying the invalid parameter. Pass the compiled expressions to the snapshot worker so DevTools does not compile them again. Valid string filters retain case-insensitive ... (Ref: https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp/pull/3030)

workarounds.symptom: Element uids returned by execute_3p_developer_tool break after one action (TextSnapshot hands out the retained extra handle)
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(snapshot): keep extra element UIDs reusable. Target files: src/TextSnapshot.ts, tests/TextSnapshot.test.ts. Extra nodes returned by third-party developer tools share their retained element handle with UID lookups. Tools dispose that handle after use, so another action on the same UID or a later snapshot fails with `Attempted to use disposed CdpElementHandle`. (Ref: https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp/pull/3493)

workarounds.symptom: Client roots from a WSL2 client are dropped by a Windows-side server (fileURLToPath ERR_INVALID_FILE_URL_PATH)
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix: accept POSIX root URIs from WSL2 clients on a Windows server. Target files: src/McpContext.ts, src/ToolHandler.ts, src/utils/files.ts. A WSL2 client that launches the server on the Windows side advertises roots like `file://[REDACTED]/project`. On Windows `fileURLToPath` throws `File URL path must be absolute`, the root is dropped, and every path inside it is denied (#2839). (Ref: https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp/pull/3380)

workarounds.symptom: CLI rejects option values that start with `-`, such as `emulate --geolocation -33.86,151.2`
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(cli): pass option values starting with `-` through to tools. Target files: src/config/cli-commands.ts, tests/cli.test.ts, tests/e2e/chrome-devtools-hyphen-positionals.test.ts. `chrome-devtools emulate 1 --geolocation -33.86,151.2` failed with `Unknown argument: 3`, so the CLI could not set a location in the southern hemisphere. `--retainedSize -1MB` and `--selfSize -1MB` (the documented upper-bound form), `--promptText "- item"` and `--submitKey -` failed the same way. Only the `=` form worked. (Ref: https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp/pull/3501)

workarounds.symptom: Tool commands fail with `Timeout waiting for daemon response` after 60 s even when the tool's own `--timeout` is longer
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix: respect tool timeouts in CLI daemon responses. Target files: src/daemon/client.ts, tests/daemon/client.test.ts. The CLI can stop waiting after 60 seconds even when a tool has a longer explicit timeout, losing the daemon's eventual result. Derive the default response deadline for `invoke_tool` from a finite positive tool timeout plus the existing 60-second response allowance. (Ref: https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp/pull/3443)

workarounds.symptom: get_console_message shows the wrong Error, or no stack, for Error arguments logged after evaluate_script
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(console): resolve Error arguments on the session of their handle. Target files: src/devtools/DevtoolsUtils.ts, src/formatters/ConsoleFormatter.ts, src/third_party/index.ts. `get_console_message` resolved an `Error` argument of a console message by sending its `objectId` to the DevTools universe's CDP session, but the `objectId` comes from the `JSHandle` that Puppeteer created on its own session. Object ids are numbered per session, so once anything wraps an object on only one of the two sessions (every... (Ref: https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp/pull/3408)

workarounds.symptom: Root plugin.json name 'chrome-devtools' diverges from marketplace entry 'chrome-devtools-mcp', breaking Codex install/upgrade
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix: align root plugin.json name with marketplace entry. Target files: plugin.json. Renames the root Agent Plugins manifest (`plugin.json`) from `chrome-devtools` to `chrome-devtools-mcp`. That matches `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.github/plugin/plugin.json`, and the plugin's entry in `claude-plugins-official`. The diff is one line. (Ref: https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp/pull/3474)

workarounds.symptom: CLI treats a running daemon as dead when process.kill(pid, 0) throws EPERM
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(cli): reuse live daemons after EPERM. Target files: src/daemon/utils.ts, tests/daemon/utils.test.ts. I changed `isDaemonRunning()` to check process identity after a signal-zero probe returns `EPERM`. Identified unrelated processes remain rejected. After `EPERM`, unavailable inspection now also counts as a running daemon. (Ref: https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp/pull/3452)

workarounds.symptom: Claude Code plugin does not load since #2696: invalid `commands` in .claude-plugin/plugin.json
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix: remove commands from claude plugin. Target files: .claude-plugin/plugin.json. Fixes https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp/issues/3468 (Ref: https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp/pull/3469)

Fix: fix: save binary request bodies byte for byte. Target files: src/formatters/NetworkFormatter.ts, tests/formatters/NetworkFormatter.test.ts. `get_network_request` with `requestFilePath` corrupts binary uploads (file uploads, protobuf/gRPC-web, msgpack). Each non-UTF-8 byte becomes U+FFFD, so the saved `.network-request` file isn't the bytes that were sent. A live 7-byte POST body (`00 9f 92 96 ff 0a 0d`) was saved as 15 bytes (`00 ef bf bd ×4 0a 0d`). (Ref: https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp/pull/3404)

workarounds.symptom: Stopping a trace with another `pageId`, or after closing the traced page, loses the recording and returns raw `Tracing.end` errors
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(performance): error when performance_stop_trace is called on a non-recording page (#2971). Target files: src/tools/ToolDefinition.ts, src/tools/performance.ts, tests/mocks.ts. Now that `McpPage.isRunningPerformanceTrace()` tracks active traces per page (`#3136`), reject `performance_stop_trace` when it is called on a page that is not recording instead of issuing `Page.stopTracing()` against that page's CDP session. When another page is currently recording, include its page ID and a `pageIdRouting`-awar... (Ref: https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp/pull/3117)
